articles.headline: The oldest grudge in football
articles.description: When Texas Tech and its brash benefactor bought their way into the college football big time, they were settling an old West Texas score.

images.name: Texas Tech [1296x729]
images.caption: Behind the vision and backing of billionaire donor Cody Campbell, coach Joey McGuire and the Red Raiders have embraced a role of disruptors as college football's villians and are trying to become a new power.

images.name: Texas Tech - Inline 1 [946x947]
images.caption: The Santa Rita No. 1 ushered in a new era of oil exploration in the Permian Basin.

images.name: Texas Tech - Inline 2 [2929x2000]
images.alt: The oil that won World War II.

images.name: Texas Tech - Inline 3 [2693x1616]
images.caption: Preston Smith (right) was the first Texas governor from West Texas. He was a student at Texas Technological College.

images.name: Texas Tech - Inline 4 [2933x1339]
images.caption: The original Four Sixes barn from 1908 is now on the Texas Tech campus at the National Ranching Heritage Center.

images.name: Texas Tech - Inline 5 [2000x3000]
images.caption: Four relief carvings on the facade of a building at Texas Tech.

images.name: Texas Tech - Inline 6 [1987x1365]
images.caption: Cody Campbell, a fourth-generation Red Raider, and his son, Carson, a 2029 recruit, talking to Pat McAfee on the "College GameDay" set.

images.name: Texas Tech - Inline 7 [2999x1940]
images.caption: Vintage oil and gas signs at Cooks Garage in Lubbock.

images.name: Texas Tech - Inline 8 [2999x1999]
images.caption: Lugene Pickering, the 1975 Texas Tech homecoming queen, has been a devoted Red Raiders fan since birth and makes a homemade cobbler for coach Joey McGuire and takes it to his house to show her appreciation after each Tech win.

images.name: Texas Tech - Inline 11 [2836x1860]

article.story: BERKELEY, Calif. -- — Micah Ford ran for two touchdowns while throwing for one and rushed for 151 yards in Stanford’s 44-26 win over California in the 129th version of the Big Game on Saturday. The junior running back scored twice early in the third quarter to help Stanford (6-5, 4-4 in Atlantic Coast Conference) pull away. Davis Warren went 14 for 25 for 214 yards and two touchdowns. Stanford is bowl eligible for the first time since 2018. “I’m extremely proud of this team,” said Stanford coach Tavita Pritchard. “I’m extremely proud of our staff and everybody involved in our program. We know that when we play Cal, the records are thrown out, and wacky stuff can happen. And I told our guys before this game, don’t expect it to be over in the first quarter, the second quarter, the third quarter, that we’re going to have to play four quarters, and that’s exactly what they did.” The Golden Bears (3-8, 2-6) opted for sophomore quarterback Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele late in the second quarter. He finished 14 for 21 with 127 yards and a touchdown. He replaced Dominic Ingrassia who played most of the first half mostly handing off. Jackson Brousseau threw a late touchdown. California coach Tosh Lapoi noted that Sagapolutele was limited in practice this week, which led to him switching to an option offense. “That’s when the monsoon was here,” he said of Wednesday’s practice.” “So we had a total of two passes that day.” Stanford led 7-0 on a 1-yard pass from Ford to tight end Chico Holt. The 13-play, 54-yard drive stayed alive with the help of a pass interference call. Cal responded with an 11-play, 75-yard drive culminating on Taimane Pucell’s 2-yard rushing touchdown. The Bears never threw on the drive. Warren rushed for an 8-yard touchdown with 5:38 left in the second to put Stanford ahead 14-7. Sagapolutele threw a 12-yard touchdown pass to Ian Strong to tie it again with 45 seconds before half. Stanford went to the half up 17-14 on a 14-yard field goal following a 52-yard fumble return from Darrius Davis. Ford scored on a 1-yard plunge early in the third. The two-point conversion failed and the lead was 23-14. Minutes later he broke free for 63 yards to account for his third touchdown. Warren found Nico Brown for 49 yards in the opening minutes of the fourth to put Stanford up 37-14. Adam Mohammed punched in a one-yard score for the Bears’ first second-half touchdown since Oct. 17. The Cardinal closed their scoring with a 48-yard Zach Giuliano touchdown reception. The takeaway Stanford: The Cardinal took the Big Game for the second straight year after having lost the previous four. It was Ford’s fourth game with at least 149 yards rushing over his last five. California: The Golden Bears have been outscored 110-14 over the past four second halves. They have been outscored 211-72 over the five-game losing streak, the program’s worst run since 2022. Up next Stanford: Hosts SMU on Saturday.
